bibliographic.title: The AI Health Arms Race: A Critical Perspective on Big Tech and the Widening Global Health Equity Gap
bibliographic.authors: Mohamed Mustaf Ahmed; Zhinya Kawa Othman
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ahmed, M. M., & Othman, Z. K. (2026). The AI health arms race: A critical perspective on Big Tech and the widening global health equity gap. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S610208

methodology.technology_context: Consumer AI health platforms integrating EHR, wearable data, and conversational AI (ChatGPT Health, Claude for Healthcare, Copilot Health, Med-Gemini, Apple Health+)

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed commentary that critically analyzes emerging AI-mediated consumer health platforms with conversational AI, LLMs, data governance, regulatory gaps, clinical safety, and human oversight in healthcare. It aligns with the review scope on governance in regulated LLM conversational systems, but it does not present original empirical methods, operational governance architecture, or primary evaluation of conversational governance mechanisms; it is better suited as contextual and policy-oriented background evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted bibliographic metadata appears corrupted in the title field; confirm full-text completeness, commentary classification, and whether later sections add empirical or implementation detail beyond the provided excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate as a critical policy commentary, but weak for empirical appraisal: no described sample, data collection protocol, or evaluative study design. Strength lies in framing equity, regulation, and oversight risks for LLM-based health conversational systems.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent and highly relevant to regulated healthcare LLM chatbots, governance, and oversight, but the commentary format provides limited direct evidence on operational conversational governance mechanisms; adequacy for answering implementation-focused review questions is therefore limited.

coding.subtheme: Global regulatory and safety gaps in Big Tech consumer health AI

human oversight for medical LLM outputs

synthesis.main_claim: The rapid 2025–2026 launch of major AI health platforms using conversational AI and LLMs may widen global health inequities unless equity-centered international and national governance, clinical safety safeguards, multilingual adaptation, and infrastructure investment are deliberately implemented.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a critical, policy-oriented landscape review of consumer AI health chatbot platforms, linking LLM clinical risks, regulatory vacuums, data sovereignty concerns, and human oversight needs to global health equity.
synthesis.limitations: Commentary without reported empirical sampling, methods, or operational governance evaluation; provided excerpts do not clearly state study limitations or detailed implementation evidence.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for governance, regulation, oversight, and risk framing in regulated healthcare conversational LLM deployments; not as central primary evidence for operational conversational governance mechanisms.
